35mm. Camera low in the dry grass, circling. Warm golden late afternoon sun, long shadows, dust.

Two boys stage a huge mock tournament fight, throwing exaggerated slow high kicks, spinning back-fists
and blocks, shouting their own sound effects.

The taller boy lands a final blow. The smaller boy performs an enormous theatrical defeat: he staggers
backward with both hands to his chest, drops slowly to his knees, sways, then falls flat on his back in
the grass, arms out, tongue out, completely still.

The taller boy immediately performs a full victory celebration over him: both fists thrown high above
his head, chest out, turning in a slow circle to an imaginary crowd, then planting one boot on the
fallen boy's chest and shouting a made-up victory cry at the sky.

The boy on the ground stays dead. Then he cracks and starts laughing.

Both faces completely free.

Audio: no music, sound effects only. Two boys shouting fight noises, a long theatrical groan of defeat,
then a huge triumphant yell, then laughing.

Negatives: no cuts, no costumes, no masks, no coloured outfits, no weapons, no logos, no legible text,
no real violence, no blood, no stretched mandated mouths, no adults, no cold light, no locked camera.

The two boys sit on a concrete step with a broken clockwork servant toy between them, a crude tin

Both boys stare at it. The smaller one leans in very close to the little face.

21mm. DUTCH CANTED LOW ANGLE from the floor among spilled sacking, tilted twenty degrees, enforcers
looming enormous against the ceiling, Viktor small between them. Camera jolts with impacts.

THE ENFORCERS NEVER SPEAK. They answer everything with violence and move without urgency.

VIKTOR: "I'm well. I'm WELL —"

He wrenches an arm loose, shoves back, connects. The enforcer does not react at all. The second
takes him by the hair, slams him face down, holds him there.

scraping. No enforcer voices.

locked camera.

VIKTOR VOICE: deep and gravelled, cracked, wrecked with pain, pitched high and desperate. Flat

Blood running from his nose across his cheek. His eye tracks across the floor and stops on the door.

A four-panel character reference sheet on a plain grey backdrop. Two boys, roughly ten years old,
shown together in all four panels: face close-ups of both, full body front, full body back, full
body side.

Rendering style: paint-on-3D in the manner of Fortiche's Arcane. Hard-edged graphic separation
between light and shadow with crisp shape breaks rather than soft blending. Skin and fabric built
from stepped planes of value with visible dry brush grain and painted tooth. Dark inked accents
along the eye line, nostril, lip line and garment seams. Visible canvas texture.

Lighting: warm pale key from the upper left, cool desaturated teal-grey shadow on the right, thin
cool rim light along the jaw and shoulder.

The whole point of this scene is that it's boring. Nobody raises their voice, nothing dramatic happens, and a man's life ends across a wooden counter in under a minute. Play it flat and it will be the most disturbing scene in the film.

Depth is built in layers: heavy lagged pipes cross the ceiling at three different heights, some
close to camera, some far. Riveted iron support arches at intervals down the length, each one
smaller than the last. Two side alcoves break the left wall, one with a stack of crates, one black
and empty. A grated floor drain in the near foreground. Damp concrete and old brick, mineral
staining, standing water reflecting the lamps.

Set into the right wall just past the steps, a heavy wooden door built from thick vertical planks
with black iron cross-bracing and heavy hinges, closed. A thin seam of warm amber light leaks around
its edges and spills in a narrow line across the wet floor.

Light: caged bulbs spaced unevenly along the ceiling, some close and bright, some far and dim, each
throwing a hard pool with long stretches of near total blackness between them. The pools get smaller
and weaker with distance. Heavy visible haze thickening toward the far end. Very low key. Restricted
palette of sick desaturated green-grey, with the warm seam around the door as the single exception.

spaced lighting, no evenly lit corridor, no bright fill, no visible far wall or dead end, no legible

A six-panel full body wardrobe reference sheet on a plain grey backdrop. Six different factory
workers, one per panel, standing front on.

Rendering style: paint-on-3D in the manner of Fortiche's Arcane. Hard-edged graphic separation
between light and shadow with crisp shape breaks rather than soft blending. Fabric, leather and
skin built from stepped planes of value with visible dry brush grain and painted tooth. Dark
inked accents along edges, folds, straps and seams. Visible canvas texture.

Lighting: warm pale key from the upper left, cool desaturated teal-grey shadow on the right, thin
cool rim light along the shoulder. Bright enough to read the clothing clearly.

These are heavy industrial workers, distinct from street civilians. Layered practical workwear,
filthy, scorched and worn through. Everything grimed with coal dust, oil and metal filings.
Muted browns, oily blacks, faded olive and washed grey. Every worker differently dressed
according to their job. Sleeves rolled or pinned, trousers tucked into boots.

Panel one, furnace man: a heavy scorched leather apron over a collarless shirt, thick leather
gauntlets to the elbow, a rag tied around the neck, dark goggles pushed up onto the forehead,
face and forearms blackened with soot.
Panel two, grinder: a short canvas work jacket with burn holes across the front, a leather half
apron, wire mesh goggles worn down over the eyes and pushed up on the head, hands wrapped in
dirty cloth strips.
Panel three, crate carrier: no jacket, a sweat-soaked undershirt, a thick padded shoulder pad
strapped across one shoulder, wide leather belt, heavy boots.
Panel four, bench assembler: a buttoned grey work coat with the sleeves cut off at the elbow,
sleeve garters, a tool roll tied at the waist, small oil-stained hands.
Panel five, a woman at the line: a shapeless buttoned overall in faded olive, hair completely
bound up in a tight headscarf, cloth wrapped around both wrists, flat worn boots.
Panel six, an older man: a patched waistcoat over a collarless shirt, a leather strap harness
across the chest, one trouser leg tied at the ankle, a flat cap black with grease.

Every worker has a small stitched numeral patch on the chest.

Every face wears the mandated expression: the mouth hauled open sideways into a hard horizontal
line, corners dragged straight back and level, lips parted showing a narrow strip of clenched
teeth, eyes forced too wide with white sclera above and below each iris, cheeks slack.

Negatives: no clean or pressed clothing, no long coats, no greatcoats, no matching uniforms, no
peaked or service caps, no clerical or office wear, no waistcoat and tie, no bound or covered
heads, no insignia, no modern safety gear, no hard hats, no hi-vis, no closed mouths, no warm
faces, no photorealism, no soft blended oil painting.

Two things that make it work. Build it in layers, so each shot adds an element and the previous ones keep running, which means it accumulates rather than just being a montage of loud noises. The horn then kills every layer at once. Total silence for a beat. That drop is the whole payoff.

A senior officer. Not tall and gaunt like the rank and file: shorter, compact, broad through the

press through underneath.

panels, in this order: head and shoulders close-up, full body front, full body back, full body
side.

Rendering style: paint-on-3D in the manner of Fortiche's Arcane. Hard-edged graphic separation
between light and shadow with crisp shape breaks rather than soft blending. Surfaces built from
stepped planes of value with visible dry brush grain and painted tooth. Dark inked accents along
edges, seams and stitching. Visible canvas texture. Strong graphic silhouette.

Lighting: warm pale key from the upper left, cool desaturated teal-grey shadow on the right, thin
cool rim light along the shoulder and the curve of the skull. Bright enough in every panel to read
the construction clearly.

A senior officer. Not tall and gaunt like the rank and file: shorter, compact, broad through the
shoulders, still and heavy. He takes up less space and is worse for it.

THE HEAD. Entirely bound, but in fine pale close-woven linen rather than coarse sackcloth, clean
and dry where the enforcers' is damp and stained. The binding has been LACQUERED HARD, a smooth
glossy shell that catches light like enamel, and MOULDED while setting into a permanent shape:
across the lower face the mandated expression is sculpted into the surface, a wide horizontal
stretched mouth with the corners hauled far back and level, formed in the hardened material
itself. No opening, no teeth, no lips, just the shape set into the shell. Above it, two shallow
sculpted hollows where eyes would be, closed over. No eye holes anywhere. The skull, brow and nose
press through underneath.

Where the enforcers' binding is soft and shapeless, his is hard, glossy and finished.

The binding is closed at the nape with a fine row of dark stitching and sealed with a small flat
brass disc pressed into the lacquer.

WARDROBE. A short fitted dark charcoal tunic buttoned to a high stiff collar, cut close, immaculate
and pressed. No greatcoat. A narrow leather belt. Thin black leather gloves. Polished boots. A
single dull brass band at each cuff, the only marking on him, no insignia and no lettering.

He carries no weapon of any kind. In one gloved hand, a slim flat leather folder.

POSTURE. Standing upright and completely still in all four panels, head level, one hand at his
side, absolutely no slouch.

Negatives: no coarse sackcloth, no damp or stained binding, no soft shapeless head, no gas mask,
no goggles, no eye holes, no visible eyes or skin, no greatcoat, no ankle-length coat, no service
cap, no peaked cap, no prod or baton or weapons, no insignia or lettering, no medals or braid, no
tall gaunt build, no photorealism, no soft blended oil painting.

A small lived-in single room in a mid-century concrete apartment block, empty of people.

Rendering style: paint-on-3D in the manner of Fortiche's Arcane. Hard-edged graphic separation
between light and shadow with crisp shape breaks rather than soft blending. Surfaces built from
stepped planes of value with visible dry brush grain and painted tooth. Dark inked accents along
edges, seams and shelf lines. Visible canvas texture.

A narrow iron bed with a worn patterned blanket and a folded jacket across the foot. A wooden
desk under the window with papers, a tin cup, a stub of pencil and a small brass desk lamp,
unlit. A wooden chair with a coat over its back. A tin basin on a stand. A threadbare rug.

Against one wall, a tall well-used wooden bookshelf packed with worn books stacked upright and
sideways, small tins, a folded cloth, a stack of loose paper tied with string.

On the middle shelf at eye level, turned to face the room and clearly the most cared-for object
in it, an award trophy: a tall upright rectangular panel of thick fluted glass with fine vertical
ribbing, seated in a heavy base of rough-hewn dark grey stone with a raw broken edge. Mounted on
the glass, a large polished dark metal glyph, a single flowing calligraphic looping curve
catching a hard highlight. On the flat front of the stone base, small crisp engraved lettering:
Higgsfield. Below it in smaller letters: GLOBAL FILM FESTIVAL.

Also on the shelves, small personal objects:

On the shelf above, slumped against the books, an old pull-string wooden cowboy doll with floppy
stuffed limbs, a wide brimmed hat, a checked shirt, and a small metal pull ring at its back.
Worn and clearly loved.

On the shelf below, a small fairground prize: two hand-carved painted wooden fighters mounted
mid-combat on a shared wooden base, one wearing a yellow cloth face mask, the other a blue cloth
face mask, both frozen in a fighting stance.

Beside them, a small tarnished brass paperweight in the shape of a castle with several tall thin
spires.

A wire face brace hangs on a nail beside the bed. A single window with rain running down it. A
heavy plank door with an iron latch.

Light: one bare bulb hanging unlit from the ceiling. The only light is cold grey spill from the
window falling across the desk and the bookshelf, catching the ribbed glass of the trophy and
throwing a hard cold highlight down the metal glyph. A thin warm line under the door. Deep
shadow in the corners. Restricted palette of sick desaturated green-grey.
